intro: Look around your home and your street. You might eat food from Mexico, wear shoes made in Vietnam and hear a song from Nigeria. People all over the world are connected. This unit helps you see how.

First, you will learn what culture is. Culture is the shared way of life of a group: its language, food, beliefs, art and manners. You will see how people learn culture, and how cultures meet and mix. Then you will take a tour of Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas.

By the end, you will be able to name the continents and read a map. You will be able to describe life in four regions. You will also be able to talk about other cultures with respect, and without stereotypes.
bigQuestion: What makes each culture special, and what do people all over the world share?

timeline.t: Cahokia grows into a large city of earth mounds in what is now Illinois
Mansa Musa of Mali travels to Mecca with great amounts of gold
Ibn Battuta writes about his travels, including his visit to Mali
The Inca build roads through the Andes Mountains
Ships from Spain reach the Americas, and colonies soon follow
The Eiffel Tower is built in Paris
The United Nations adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
Senegal and many other African countries become independent
The European Union is formed by countries in Europe
India passes China as the country with the most people

words.d: the way of life a group of people shares, like its language, food, beliefs and art
a habit or way of doing something that a group shares
a way of doing things passed down from older people to younger people
a person who moves to live in a new country
when groups share and trade ideas, foods, words and art
one of the very large pieces of land on Earth
an unfair idea that all people in a group are the same
the number of people who live in a place
a group of lands and peoples ruled by one leader
the first peoples to live in a place, and their descendants today
land ruled by a country that is far away

choices: The shared way of life of a group
test.why: Culture is the way of life a group shares, like language, food, beliefs and art.

test.q: How do people get their culture?
choices: They learn it from family, friends and school
They find it on a globe
They choose it once a year
test.why: Culture is learned by watching, listening and being taught.

test.q: Deep-dish pizza in Chicago came from a food first made in...
test.why: Pizza first came from Italy, and Chicago cooks made a new deep-dish kind.

choices: A word used only in math
A word one language takes from another
test.why: A loanword is a word taken from another language, like safari from Swahili.

test.q: Why do some students learn that there are six continents?
choices: They count North and South America as one
test.why: In many Latin American countries, North and South America are counted as one continent.

choices: A true fact about one person
An unfair idea that all people in a group are the same
test.why: A stereotype treats everyone in a group as the same, which is unfair.

test.q: Why does a flat map stretch some places?
choices: Earth is round, and a flat page cannot show it perfectly
test.why: Like an orange peel pressed flat, a round Earth must stretch to fit on a flat page.

test.q: Which continent is the largest and has the most people?
test.why: Asia is the largest continent, with about 4.7 billion people.

test.q: What money do many European Union countries share?
test.why: Many members of the European Union use the euro.

test.q: Which country passed China in population in 2023?
test.why: India passed China in 2023 to become the country with the most people.

test.q: The Mali Empire grew rich from trade in...
test.why: Mali traded gold and salt carried across the Sahara.

choices: The largest hot desert in the world
test.why: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, in North Africa.

test.q: Where did people build large earth mounds in Illinois long ago?
test.why: People built great earth mounds at Cahokia, near today's St. Louis.

test.q: Why do most people in Mexico speak Spanish?
choices: Mexico was once a colony of Spain
test.why: Spain ruled Mexico as a colony, and its language stayed.

test.q: What did Marco and the four pen pals both show?
choices: Every family lives the same way
People everywhere share family, food and customs, in their own ways
test.why: Both stories show that people around the world share family and food, each in their own way.

write.prompt: Are people around the world more alike or more different? Make a claim. Use two or three facts from this unit, such as the pen pals, cultural exchange in Chicago, or the continents you toured, and explain how they support your claim.
tips: Start with one clear sentence that states your claim.
Name two or three facts or stories from the unit.
Say how people are alike and how they are different, fairly.
Use unit words like culture, custom and stereotype.
End by saying what you learned.
